data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Back
data.comment: Note on the arrow that goes back to the screen before.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Close
data.comment: Note on the same arrow on the first screen, where there is nothing to go back to.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Undo
data.comment: Note on the undo arrow. {action} is what undoing takes back, such as "rename".

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Redo
data.comment: Note on the redo arrow. {action} is what redoing does again, such as "rename".

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Refresh
data.value: Read the ship again, in case somebody has changed a button
data.comment: Note on the button that reads the blocks again.

data.name: Sprocket.Rename.Empty
data.comment: Said under a name being typed, when it is empty and the thing must have a name.

data.name: Sprocket.Rename.Taken
data.comment: Said under a name being typed, when something else already has it.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Broken
data.value: **Something needs mending** Open it to see what.
data.comment: Note on a row's light when it is red.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Ran
data.comment: Note on a row's light while it flashes, just after the thing ran.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Idle
data.value: **Idle** Lights green when it runs, and red when something in it needs mending.
data.comment: Note on a row's light when it is dark.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Delete
data.comment: Note on a row's bin.

data.name: Sprocket.Switch.On
data.comment: The half of an on/off switch that turns something on. Short: it shares the switch with the next.

data.name: Sprocket.Switch.Off
data.comment: The half of an on/off switch that turns something off.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOn
data.comment: Note on a switch that is off.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOff
data.comment: Note on a switch that is on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOn
data.comment: Note on a logic system's switch when it is off.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOff
data.value: Switch the whole system off, stopping every sequence in it
data.comment: Note on a logic system's switch when it is on.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Title
data.comment: Heading of the first screen. {name} is the grid's name, which is pressed to rename it, so the words either side of it are drawn around it, and the name is always shown exactly as it is.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NameAbout
data.value: This grid's name, the one the game shows for it everywhere. Press to rename the grid.
data.comment: Note on the grid's name in the heading.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.New
data.comment: Button, after a plus that means add, that adds a new logic system. A logic system is a set of sequences that work together, such as an airlock's.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NewAbout
data.value: Start a new logic system on this grid.
data.comment: Note on the button above.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Load
data.comment: Button that opens the blueprint library, where blueprints are imported and exported. Also the library's heading.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.LoadAbout
data.value: The library of **blueprints**, where they are imported and exported.
data.comment: Note on the button above.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Empty
data.comment: Said where the list of logic systems would be, when there are none.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.MakeBlueprint
data.comment: Button on a logic system's row that makes it a blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.MakeBlueprintAbout
data.value: Turn this into a **blueprint**, so more logic systems like it can be made, each using its own blocks. This one becomes the first of them.
data.comment: Note on the button above.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.MadeFrom
data.comment: Heading over the logic systems made from one blueprint. {name} is the blueprint's name, as the player gave it.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Edit
data.comment: Button beside the heading over the logic systems made from one blueprint, which opens the blueprint's logic system screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.EditBlueprint
data.value: Opens the **{name}** blueprint, to change what starts its sequences and what they do. Every logic system made from it changes with it.
data.comment: Note on the Edit blueprint button. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.LibraryUnbuilt
data.value: Not built yet. Blueprints will be imported and exported here.
data.comment: Said on the blueprint library while it is not built.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.AddAnother
data.comment: Row under the logic systems made from a blueprint, after a plus that means add, which makes one more. The blueprint is named in the heading above, so the row does not name it.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.AddAnotherAbout
data.value: Make another logic system from the **{name}** blueprint, and choose which blocks it uses.
data.comment: Note on the row above. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Running
data.comment: Said on a logic system's row while any of its sequences runs.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Numbered
data.comment: What a logic system is called when it has no name and its blocks share none. {number} is its number.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Instance
data.comment: What one of the logic systems made from a blueprint is called when it has no name of its own. {name} is the blueprint's, {number} which one it is.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.System
data.comment: Asked before a logic system is deleted, with its name under it.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Blueprint
data.value: This deletes the {name} blueprint and every logic system made from it, and cannot be undone. Type {name} to go ahead.
data.comment: Over the box a blueprint's name is typed into to delete it; the button beside the box does nothing until the name is typed. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Instance
data.comment: Asked before one of the logic systems made from a blueprint is deleted, with its name under it. Only that one goes.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.InstanceKept
data.value: The {name} blueprint and the other logic systems made from it are kept. This cannot be undone.
data.comment: Said on the answer that deletes one of the logic systems made from a blueprint. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Keep
data.comment: The answer that deletes nothing.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Confirm
data.comment: The answer that deletes it.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Final
data.comment: Said on the answer that deletes.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NameAbout
data.value: This logic system's name. Press to rename it.
data.comment: Note on a logic system's name, in the heading of its own screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Blueprint
data.comment: Said after a blueprint's name in the heading of its screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Delete
data.comment: Note on the bin in the header of a logic system's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.DeleteBlueprint
data.value: Delete this blueprint, and every logic system made from it
data.comment: Note on the bin in the header of a blueprint's logic system screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.EditPanel
data.comment: Button on a blueprint's logic system screen that opens the panel its blocks are chosen on, to set up its slots and description.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Using
data.comment: Leads the name of the logic system whose blocks every sentence on the screen names: the system's own, or for a blueprint a list of the blocksets made from it.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Triggers
data.comment: Heading over a logic system's triggers: what starts its sequences.

data.name: Sprocket.System.When
data.comment: Button that adds a trigger started by something happening to a block.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Every
data.comment: Button that adds a trigger started on a timer.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Sequences
data.comment: Heading over a logic system's sequences: the named runs of steps its triggers start.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NewSequence
data.comment: Button, after a plus that means add, that adds a sequence with nothing to start it yet.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NoSequences
data.comment: Said in place of the list of sequences while a logic system has none.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Copy
data.value: Creates a copy of this sequence, switched off and with no trigger of its own
data.comment: Note on the copy mark of a sequence that a trigger starts.

data.name: Sprocket.System.CopyUnstarted
data.value: Creates a copy of this sequence, switched off
data.comment: Note on the copy mark of a sequence nothing starts.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Live
data.comment: Badge on a trigger while what it watches for is true at this instant, such as a door standing open.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Delete
data.comment: Note on the bin at the end of a trigger's row.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.NameAbout
data.value: This sequence's name. Press to rename it.
data.comment: Note on a sequence's name, in the heading of its own screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DoSomething
data.comment: Button under a sequence's steps, after a plus that means add, that adds a step acting on blocks. The ellipsis says it asks which before it adds.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Wait
data.comment: Button under a sequence's steps, after a plus that means add, that adds a step waiting a length of time. The ellipsis says it asks how long before it adds.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Locked
data.value: Switched on. Switch it off to make changes.
data.comment: Said in place of the buttons that add steps while the sequence is switched on.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Held
data.comment: Said in place of the buttons that add steps while another player is editing. {holder} is that player's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Delete
data.comment: Note on the bin beside a sequence's switch.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DeleteQuestion
data.comment: Asked before a sequence is deleted, with what it does under it.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DeleteStep
data.comment: Note on the bin at the end of a step's row.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedBusy
data.comment: Said while a sequence was started and did not run because it was already running. {busy} is how many times.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedOff
data.comment: Said while a sequence was started and did not run because it was switched off. {off} is how many times.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedBoth
data.comment: The two above at once.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SwitchOnQuestion
data.comment: Asked on leaving a sequence that was changed and is still switched off.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SwitchItOn
data.comment: The answer that switches the sequence on.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.LeaveItOff
data.comment: The answer that leaves the sequence switched off.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitQuestion
data.comment: Title of the question that chooses how long a waiting step waits.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Different
data.value: This block holds a program from a different version.
data.comment: Banner on the first screen when the block's program was written by a version that cannot be read.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.DifferentDetail
data.value: This version cannot read it, so this screen starts empty. The block still holds it until you change something here - and that replaces it for good.
data.comment: Shown when the banner above is opened.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Partial
data.value: This block holds a program that could only partly be read.
data.comment: Banner on the first screen when only part of the block's program could be read.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.PartialDetail
data.value: What could be read is shown here. The block still holds the whole of it until you change something here - and that replaces it with what you see.
data.comment: Shown when the banner above is opened.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Trouble
data.comment: Shown under the banner's detail. {trouble} is what went wrong, in the reader's own words, which are not translated.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Replace
data.comment: Button that replaces the program that could not be read, on the banner and as an answer to the question below.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Question
data.value: Replace the program this block holds? The one that could not be read will be gone.
data.comment: Asked before the first change that replaces a program that could not be read.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Keep
data.comment: Answer to the question above that changes nothing.

data.name: Sprocket.Lease.Holder
data.comment: Banner when somebody else is editing the same block. {holder} is their name.

data.name: Sprocket.Lease.Detail
data.value: Only one person can edit at a time. Reopen this once they're done to make changes.
data.comment: Shown when the banner above is opened.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Search
data.comment: Hint in the box that narrows a column of a pick, or its list of kinds, by typing.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Done
data.comment: Button that finishes a pick.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Back
data.comment: Note on the column that turns a pick back to its page before.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Next
data.comment: Note on the column that turns a pick on to its page after.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ClearTyped
data.comment: Note on the cross that empties a box that narrows a list.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.EveryKind
data.comment: Note on the cross that takes away the kind a list of blocks is narrowed to.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.AllShown
data.comment: Line over a list of blocks showing every one. {count} is how many.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SomeShown
data.comment: Line over a list of blocks narrowed to some of them. {shown} is how many are shown, {count} how many there are.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Anything
data.comment: The entry in the list of kinds that narrows to no kind at all.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KeepQuestion
data.comment: Asked on leaving a pick that has changed what it opened on.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KeepThem
data.comment: Answer to the question above that finishes the pick.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.DiscardThem
data.comment: Answer to the question above that leaves without finishing.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Blocks
data.comment: Title of the column of blocks in a pick.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NoBlocksHappen
data.value: Nothing here has anything that can happen to it.
data.comment: Where the column of blocks is empty, picking what starts something.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NoBlocksDone
data.value: Nothing here has anything that can be done to it.
data.comment: Where the column of blocks is empty, picking what a step does.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatHappens
data.comment: Title of the column of what can happen to the blocks picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatToDo
data.comment: Title of the column of what can be done to the blocks picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NothingHappens
data.value: Those blocks have nothing in common that can happen to them.
data.comment: Where the column of what happens is empty.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NothingDone
data.value: Those blocks have nothing in common that can be done to them.
data.comment: Where the column of what to do is empty.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatItDoes
data.comment: Title of the column choosing what a trigger does.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NonePicked
data.comment: Under the column of blocks, where none is picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.OnePicked
data.comment: Under the column of blocks, where one is picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SomePicked
data.comment: Under the column of blocks, where several are picked. {count} is how many.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.AnyOne
data.comment: Choice over the blocks that any one of them is enough.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.AllOfThem
data.comment: Choice over the blocks that all of them are needed together.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Values
data.comment: Heading over a block's values, in the terminal's way of listing what it offers.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ToolbarActions
data.comment: Heading over a block's actions, in the terminal's way of listing what it offers.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Organized
data.comment: Tab showing what a block offers as Sprocket groups and words it.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Terminal
data.comment: Tab showing what a block offers as the block itself declares it.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Shared
data.value: Currently showing only what the selected blocks share
data.comment: Note over what several blocks offer.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Pending
data.value: Sprocket has not checked this block yet, so some of what it offers may be doubled, missing or oddly named.
data.comment: Note over what a block offers, before the block has been checked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Partial
data.value: Sprocket has only partly checked this block, so some of what it offers may still be doubled, missing or oddly named.
data.comment: Note over what a block offers, where the block has been checked in part.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Waits
data.value: This takes time to finish. The sequence waits until it is done before going on to the next step.
data.comment: Note on the mark beside something done that a step waits for.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Run
data.comment: Choice that a trigger runs the sequence chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Stop
data.comment: Choice that a trigger stops the sequence chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SingleAction
data.comment: Choice that a trigger does one thing to some blocks, chosen on the page after.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NewSequence
data.comment: Choice that a trigger runs a sequence made for it.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Sequences
data.comment: Heading over the sequences a trigger may run or stop.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.HowOftenQuestion
data.comment: Title of the page choosing how often a timer fires.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.HowOften
data.comment: Title of the column of rates a timer fires at.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.EveryTick
data.comment: The fastest rate a timer fires at.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Rate
data.comment: A rate a timer fires at. {name} is its word, such as steady; {ticks} how many ticks apart.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameAbout
data.value: This blueprint's name. Press to rename it.
data.comment: Note on a blueprint's name at the head of its screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Parts
data.comment: Heading over a blueprint's slots, where each is filled with blocks.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Panel
data.comment: Heading of a blueprint's configuration panel while it is being set up: the slots and words everyone filling a blockset made from the blueprint sees.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.PanelFor
data.comment: After "Configuration panel" in its heading. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.PanelAbout
data.value: Shown to anyone setting up, or changing, something made from this blueprint.
data.comment: Under the heading of a configuration panel being set up.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.StillOne
data.comment: Beside the heading over a blockset's slots, where one slot that needs a block has none.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.StillMany
data.comment: Beside the heading over a blockset's slots. {count} is how many slots that need a block have none, always more than one.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.From
data.comment: After the name of a logic system made from a blueprint, at the head of its slots. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Gone
data.comment: Beside a slot whose block is no longer on the construct. {name} is what the block was called.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Description
data.comment: Heading over the box a blueprint's description is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.DescriptionHint
data.value: What this blueprint does, and what whoever fills it in needs to know.
data.comment: In the empty box a blueprint's description is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.AboutHint
data.comment: In the empty box what a slot is for is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Preview
data.comment: Button that shows rich text as it will read, in place of the box it is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Edit
data.comment: Button that goes back from rich text's preview to the box it is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Markup
data.comment: Button that shows, beside a box rich text is written in, the marks it can be written with.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Examples
data.value: **strong words** *emphasized words* # A heading - An item in a list 1. A counted item `code` ---
data.comment: The guide to the marks rich text can be written with, one example per line, each shown as typed and then as it reads. Translate the words, and keep the marks: ** * # - 1. ` ---

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.ExamplesNote
data.value: A blank line starts a new paragraph. A \ before a mark shows the mark itself.
data.comment: Under the guide to the marks rich text can be written with.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Required
data.comment: On the switch of a slot that must be filled with a block. The other side reads optional.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Optional
data.comment: After the name of a slot that may be left without a block.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NoneFits
data.value: Nothing on this construct can fill it.
data.comment: Where no block on the construct can fill a part.

data.name: Sprocket.Prompt.Continue
data.comment: Button beside a box a name is typed into, that gives it.
